article.title: Respond to a data request about a recipient
article.excerpt: What the platform holds about a message, what it deliberately does not, and where the data subject relationship actually sits.

p: The message log stores metadata: the time, the destination number, the tenant, the provider, the sender identity, the normalized status, the provider message ID and the raw error code. Credentials are stored encrypted, and suppression records hold the judgment plus the minimum audit detail needed to explain it.

sections.h: What it deliberately does not hold
p: Message bodies are not persisted. This is a deliberate compliance decision: a body is a real conversation, and retaining it would create retention, export and deletion obligations that metadata does not — for a benefit that amounts to one more readable column.
sections.note: Practically, that means a request for "the content of the messages you sent me" cannot be answered from the platform log. If you need content for your own records, your system has to keep it.

steps.p: Match on the destination number in international format.

steps.h: Filter the log to that number
steps.p: Read the metadata rows: when, which channel, which sender, what status.
If the number opted out, the suppression entry is the audit trail for that decision.

steps.h: Answer from your own records for content
steps.p: Content, consent evidence and the commercial relationship are yours, not the platform’s.

p: The relationship with the recipient is yours, so the request is answered by you. The platform processes the metadata on your instruction and does not decide who may be messaged — nothing on this page is legal advice about how your obligations apply.
